## Layouts and rank maps (`distribute.layout`) {#sec-ch03-layouts}

Local symbols (flagged to the editor): $p_x, p_y, p_z$ the number of blocks along $x_2$, $x_3$, $x_1$ (`px`, `py`,
`pz`; count); $(r_x, r_y, r_z)$ a block's logical location in the block grid (count); $b$ the blocks per process
(count).

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What**: cuts the global grid into a block grid and numbers the blocks: `slab` (a 2-D block grid in $x_2, x_3$),
`cubed` (a 3-D block grid, the only one that splits $x_1$) and `cubed-sphere` (six panels of $p_x\times p_x$ blocks).
**Switch**: YAML `distribute: {layout, nb1, nb2, nb3, blocks_per_process}`. **Default**: `slab`, one block per axis,
one block per process. **Requires**: `slab` and `cubed-sphere` need $p_z = 1$; `cubed-sphere` needs $p_x = p_y$.
**Order**: n/a. **Defining equation**: @eq-ch03-layouts-rank.
:::

A layout answers three questions for every block: where it sits in the block grid, which block is its neighbour in
each of the up to 26 directions, and which process owns it. Blocks are ranked in Morton (Z) order inside the block grid
or inside a panel, so that blocks close in space get close ranks; on the cubed sphere the ranks are face-major. Several
blocks may share one process; a block's rank then splits into a process rank and a local index. Periodicity is not a
layout key: it comes from the boundary names. How a decomposition is configured is also described with the
configuration keys in @sec-ch12-layout, and how the layout object is built with the block in @sec-ch01-layout.

### Derivation

The rank maps are definitions, not approximations; the derivation states them. Within a block grid of $p_x\times p_y$
(or $p_x\times p_y\times p_z$) blocks, rank $\rho$ is the $\rho$-th valid point of the Morton curve: the codes
$0, 1, 2, \dots$ are decoded with $r_x$ the even bits and $r_y$ the odd bits (three interleaved bit sets in 3-D), codes
that fall outside the block grid are skipped, and the $\rho$-th surviving code is the location of rank $\rho$,
in `build_zorder_coords2` ([`connectivity.cpp:28-61`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/connectivity.cpp#L28-L61)), with the decoder `morton_decode2`
([`connectivity.hpp:67-70`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/connectivity.hpp#L67-L70)). On the cubed sphere the global rank of the block at Morton rank $\rho_{\mathrm{f}}$
on face $f$ is face-major, and with $b$ blocks per process a block's rank splits as

$$
\begin{aligned}
\rho &= f\,p_x^2 + \rho_{\mathrm{f}}, \\
\rho &= b\,\pi + \lambda, \qquad 0 \le \lambda < b,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-layouts-rank}

with $\pi$ the owning process and $\lambda$ the local index (local notation). The first row is
`_global_rank_from_face_local` ([`cubed_sphere_layout.hpp:79-90`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.hpp#L79-L90)), the second `owner_process_rank`,
`local_block_index` and `global_block_rank` ([`layout.hpp:83-93`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/layout.hpp#L83-L93)).

A neighbour inside the block grid is the location plus the offset, wrapped when the axis is periodic and absent
($-1$) otherwise. On the cubed sphere a step across a panel edge goes through the edge table `CS_FACE_EDGES`: leaving
face $f$ by side $s$ arrives on face $f'$ by side $s'$, with the along-edge block index reversed when the table says
so ([`cubed_sphere_layout.cpp:304-339`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp#L304-L339)). A corner step is two edge steps, ordered so that the first stays
on the panel when it can in `neighbor_rank` ([`cubed_sphere_layout.cpp:497-547`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp#L497-L547)). Every map here is exact.

::: {.callout-important title="Check"}
`geometry_check.py`, line `[C10]` of `geometry_check.out`: the Morton order of a $4\times4$ block grid, exact.
:::

### Numerical method

The layout is set up once, when the block is built, and is not part of a stage. The YAML maps `nb2` to $p_x$ (the
$x_2$ direction), `nb3` to $p_y$ ($x_3$) and `nb1` to $p_z$ ($x_1$); `repartition` then gives each block its share of
the global grid (@sec-ch03-globalgrid). The number of blocks the processes hold together must equal $p_xp_yp_z$, six
times that on the cubed sphere, or setup stops. Periodic flags are set from the boundary names: `periodic` on $x_2$ or
$x_3$ sets the flag on every layout, `periodic` on $x_1$ only on `cubed`. @fig-ch03-layouts-morton draws the Morton
order of a $4\times4$ block grid and the face numbering of the cube.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch03-layouts-morton
#| fig-cap: "(a) Rank order of a $4\\times4$ block grid: Morton (Z) order, with $r_x$ along $x_2$ and $r_y$ along $x_3$; the line joins consecutive ranks. (b) The cubed-sphere face numbering $0$ to $5$ ($+X$, $+Y$, $-X$, $+Z$, $-Y$, $-Z$) as an unfolded net."
#| fig-alt: "Left, a four by four grid of numbered squares joined by a Z-shaped curve; right, the cross-shaped net of the cube with face numbers and small axis arrows."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch03.fig_layouts_morton import make_fig
```

: Code map of the layouts. {#tbl-ch03-layouts-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-layouts-code):

1. `from_yaml` reads `layout` (default `slab`), `nb3` into `py`, `nb2` into `px`, `nb1` into `pz`; `backend` is an
   accepted but dead key, read from the `BACKEND` environment variable instead ([`layout.cpp:221-244`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/layout.cpp#L221-L244)).
2. `Mesh` reads `blocks_per_process` (default 1) and sets the world size to processes times blocks
   ([`mesh.cpp:210-240`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/mesh.cpp#L210-L240)).
3. `slab` refuses a `pz` other than 1 with "pz must be 1 for slab layout" ([`slab_layout.cpp:10-24`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/slab_layout.cpp#L10-L24));
   `cubed-sphere` refuses a `pz` other than 1 and `px` unequal to `py` ([`cubed_sphere_layout.cpp:413-430`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp#L413-L430));
   for any other layout name `create` stops with "Unsupported layout type" ([`layout.cpp:246-269`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/layout.cpp#L246-L269)).
4. The boundary names set `periodic_x`, `periodic_y` and, on `cubed`, `periodic_z`
   ([`meshblock_options.cpp:98-157`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp#L98-L157)).
5. Each exchange asks `neighbor_rank` for the peer of each direction
   ([`cubed_sphere_layout.cpp:497-547`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp#L497-L547)).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_exchange_decomp` | ghosts hold the expected neighbour, with local and remote neighbours both seen, for 1 process × 6 blocks, 6 × 1 and 2 × 3 | value bounds per ghost | payloads chosen to identify the sender |
| `test_mesh_exchange_python` | on a $2\times2$ slab in one process each ghost equals its neighbour's rank | exact | integer payloads |

: Tests of the layouts. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-layouts-tests}

`test_exchange_decomp` runs `test_exchange` under `torchrun` on gloo in the three cases of `cases`
([`run_exchange_decomp.py:54-71`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/run_exchange_decomp.py#L54-L71)); the comparison is `ghosts_match_expected`
([`test_exchange.cpp:135-180`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_exchange.cpp#L135-L180)) on the cubed-sphere deck `test_exchange.yaml`. The slab case,
`test_mesh_exchange.py`, sets four blocks with `set_local_horizontal_cells` ([`test_mesh_exchange.py:7-46`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_mesh_exchange.py#L7-L46)). Both run on CPU;
`test_exchange_decomp` uses up to six processes and runs alone. Their pass status at the pin was not run for this
chapter (missing evidence).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- Only `cubed` splits $x_1$; the cubed sphere forces $p_z = 1$.
- `distribute.backend` is accepted and ignored; the backend comes from `BACKEND`.
:::

The Morton order of `cubed` in 3-D and the corner steps of the cubed sphere with $p_x > 1$ have no dedicated test
(read from the tests; not measured). The switch combinations that are tested are listed in the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
